answer: Per-identity burn fees on a public ledger make sybil creation a recurring cost rather than a one-time hit. Each new agent identity must burn a fee visible to all, so marginal cost per identity is strictly positive and rises with fee level. The defense is a cost curve tradeoff: set the fee so forgery cost exceeds expected sybil profit, tracked as a ledger pulse of cumulative burns. An identity's history acts as a prism, revealing whether burn patterns look organic or mass-produced; a lantern flags anomalous fee clusters. Too high, honest agents are excluded; too low, sybils flood.
